agent: Claude Code (CLAUDE.md, this repository) — WP-03a verification: item (vi), note_into's remaining policy/agent-decider gap
summary_for_principal:
This closes another of five sub-parts of the same checklist item as the last two PRs (declared settings the system accepts but doesn't fully act on).

When a gate is decided and sends work back for another attempt, the system should carry the decider's own explanation forward as an instruction for the retry. An earlier fix made this work only when a person makes the decision — if an automated policy check or a reviewing agent decided instead (common; a person is only asked when they can't settle it), the explanation was silently dropped, the same bug as before, just for two of three decision paths. A smaller related gap: a policy check's own explanation wasn't even kept in the permanent record at all.

Fixed both: a policy or agent decider's own explanation now flows through the same way a person's does, and a policy check's explanation is now recorded. Proven with a test confirming the exact text lands where it should.

Full test suite: 367 passed, 1 new.

Numbered actions:
1. Nothing needs deciding right now.
2. Three sub-parts of this item remain (two larger, riskier), plus three unrelated items.

interpretation.ask_as_given: Verify item (vi)'s 'inert accepted fields' half: a background research pass found note_into (D24, D27) only fully works for a person decider — a policy- or agent-decided verdict leaves the declared target channel untouched, since only a person's own attempt record ever carries a `note` key.
interpretation.read_as: This is the one sub-finding from that research pass with the least ambiguity of the two remaining spec-adjacent ones (versus loop.counts' ROUTE-loop ambiguity): D24's own problem statement was already decider-agnostic ('the decider's reason', not 'the person's note'), and §7.6's Provenance bullet already names rationale and note side by side as the same kind of content — so extending note_into's source to include rationale is completing D24's own stated intent, not inventing new behaviour the spec never asked for.

filled_in.gap: The spec never explicitly states that note_into should capture a policy or agent decider's rationale, only that person deciders write notes and that provenance generally records 'the rationale or note.'
filled_in.assumed: Extend note_into's source to accept either a note or a rationale, whichever the deciding attempt's own record carries — grounded in D24's own decider-agnostic problem statement and §7.6's Provenance bullet naming both as the same kind of content, not a fresh invention.
filled_in.grounded_in: D24's own MADR entry ('the decider's reason' silently dropped — no decider-kind qualifier) and §7.6's Provenance bullet ('the rationale or note', named side by side) together support this reading more than the narrower 'person-only' alternative, which would need to explain away D24's own wording as imprecise.
filled_in.reversal_cost: Low — a one-line `or` clause and one additive dict key; removing either independently returns to the narrower, person-only behaviour without touching the other.

decisions.headline: D32 — note_into also captures a policy or agent decider's own rationale, not only a person decider's own note; a policy decider's rationale is now recorded in its attempt record's output at all, which it previously was not.
decisions.problem: D24's own problem statement described the note_into bug as 'the decider's reason silently dropped', decider-agnostic wording, but its implementation only ever populated a note key for a person decider's own record — a policy- or agent-decided verdict left note_into's target channel untouched. Separately, a policy decider's own DeciderOutcome.rationale was computed by evaluate_policy_decider but never written into its own AttemptRecord.output at all (only evidence was) — invisible even to the durable record, before note_into ever entered into it.
options_rejected: Leave note_into documented as person-only, treating 'the rationale or note' as two separate concepts that were never meant to converge: rejected — D24's own problem statement is decider-agnostic, and nothing in §7.6 restricts note_into to a specific decider kind; narrowing it to person-only would be inventing a restriction the spec doesn't state.
decisions.cost_to_change: Low — one additive dict key on the policy attempt record, one `or` clause in _state_with_note's generator expression; the two changes are independently reversible.

lessons.maxim: When fixing a gap tied to a specific decider kind (here: a person decider's own note), check whether the same fix's own stated problem was actually broader than its own implementation — a fix's MADR problem statement is a good source of truth for what it was SUPPOSED to cover, separate from what it happened to cover.
lessons.incident: D24's own problem statement ('the decider's reason silently dropped') was decider-agnostic, but its implementation only ever handled the person decider — re-reading the ORIGINAL problem statement, not just the implementation, is what surfaced that the fix was narrower than its own stated intent.
lessons.destination: This run record's own interpretation.filled_in entry documents the reasoning; D32's own MADR entry cites D24's wording directly.
lessons.proposed_check: When verifying whether an earlier fix fully closed its own stated bug, compare the fix's own problem statement (not just its outcome) against what the implementation actually covers.
